html:
The Q'ero are a Quechua-speaking community in the mountains of Paucartambo province, east of Cusco in Peru. Their villages spread from high llama and alpaca pastures down to warm valleys where they grow maize, a way of using many altitudes that goes back to the Inca and before.

Living far from roads, they kept many old Andean customs and weaving designs. They became widely known after a 1955 expedition led by the Cusco anthropologist Oscar Núñez del Prado, which first published their version of the myth of Inkarrí, the Inca king who will one day return. Since then they have drawn visitors interested in Andean spirituality. See also Quechua and Peru.
